_readme: Single editable content record for the site. Every fact carries a `status`. confirmed = approved by Dr. Abela or office staff (only these appear in a production build). public = corroborated in public sources, awaiting practice confirmation (shown in staging builds with a marker). lead = secondary source only (never rendered; listed in the content-gaps report). missing = not yet supplied (staging shows a placeholder; production omits). `source` cites the research handoff reference numbers.

shortBio.value: Oliver G. Abela, MD, FACC, is a Tampa cardiologist with fellowship training in cardiovascular disease, interventional cardiology, and advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology. His background includes complex coronary intervention, structural heart procedures, and cardiovascular imaging. He earned his medical degree at Michigan State University and completed postgraduate training in Michigan, Ohio, Nevada, and Arizona.

areasOfCare.title: Coronary artery disease
areasOfCare.summary: Chest pain, shortness of breath with exertion, prior heart attack, and blocked or narrowed heart arteries.
areasOfCare.detail: Care starts with evaluation and a treatment plan, which may include medications, risk-factor management, and testing. When a blockage needs treatment, Dr. Abela's training includes coronary stenting (PCI), complex and high-risk PCI, and chronic total occlusion (CTO) procedures.
areasOfCare.settingNote: Catheter-based procedures are done in a hospital catheterization lab, not in the office.

areasOfCare.title: Advanced heart failure
areasOfCare.summary: Weakened or stiff heart muscle, fluid buildup, and heart failure that is difficult to control.
areasOfCare.detail: Dr. Abela completed dedicated fellowship training in advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology. Management focuses on optimizing medications, monitoring, and coordinating hospital-level care when it is needed.
areasOfCare.settingNote: Which monitoring services are available through the office has not been confirmed.

areasOfCare.title: Structural heart and valve disease
areasOfCare.summary: Narrowed or leaking heart valves, holes in the heart (ASD/PFO), and stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
areasOfCare.detail: His procedural background includes transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), transcatheter mitral repair (MitraClip), ASD/PFO closure, and left atrial appendage closure (Watchman). An office visit helps determine whether a procedure is appropriate.
areasOfCare.settingNote: These procedures are performed in the hospital.

areasOfCare.title: Cardiac imaging
areasOfCare.summary: Echocardiography (heart ultrasound) and cardiac CT to look at the heart's structure and function.
areasOfCare.detail: Dr. Abela holds credentials in echocardiography and cardiovascular CT, and he uses imaging to guide diagnosis and procedure planning.
areasOfCare.settingNote: Whether testing is done in the office or at an outside facility has not been confirmed.

areasOfCare.title: Prevention and cholesterol management
areasOfCare.summary: High cholesterol, family history of heart disease, and lowering future cardiovascular risk.
areasOfCare.detail: With a clinical lipidology credential and research on plaque biology, Dr. Abela can address cholesterol and risk-factor management as part of long-term heart care.

areasOfCare.title: Cardiogenic shock and circulatory support
areasOfCare.summary: Critical heart failure that needs temporary mechanical support of the circulation.
areasOfCare.detail: This is hospital-based expertise, including Impella-supported procedures. It is not an office service.

areasOfCare.title: Pulmonary embolism intervention
areasOfCare.summary: Catheter-based removal of blood clots in the lungs.
areasOfCare.detail: Listed as a clinical interest (mechanical thrombectomy).
areasOfCare.note: Confirm this is still part of his current clinical work.

trials.name: DRAIN-HF
trials.summary: A clinical trial evaluating an investigational device, the Aortix system, for patients hospitalized with acute heart failure. The device is investigational. It is not an approved routine treatment.
trials.note: Confirm recruitment status and whether the independent office has a role before publishing.
